# Mathematical Conjectures and Open Problems

### AI's Top 100 and a Three-Volume Research Collection

Start with 100 major problems, then explore three companion volumes of mathematical conjectures, open problems, and original research leads.

**Generated by AI under the direction of Shen Yang, a Chinese interdisciplinary scholar and AI enthusiast.** This repository contains four Chinese-language PDFs: the Top 100 edition dated October 24, 2026, and three companion volumes compiled on October 25, 2026. The Markdown documentation is available in English and Simplified Chinese; the PDFs are in Chinese, with source material also appearing in English and LaTeX.

[Top 100](AI_Top_100_Mathematical_Conjectures_CN.pdf) · [Complete 100-Entry Catalog](CATALOG.md) · [Volume I](math_conjectures_census_2026-10-25.pdf) · [Volume II](math_conjectures_volume_2_supplement_2026-10-25.pdf) · [Volume III](math_conjectures_volume_3_supplement_2026-10-25.pdf)

## Suggested Reading Paths

1. **Explore major mathematical problems.** Begin with the Top 100 editorial notes and status legend, then choose entries from the [Markdown catalog](CATALOG.md).
2. **Understand the scale and counting methods.** Read Volume I's conclusions, definitions, and counting rules before examining individual records.
3. **Find additional research leads.** Use Volume II's catalog excerpts and formalized statements, followed by Volume III's multi-source records and parameterized-problem appendix.
4. **Prepare a research proposal or literature review.** Record each candidate problem's source identifier, full assumptions, version, and status. Verify these against the original paper or source page before defining a research question.

### Interpreting Rankings and Research Status

- The ranking is an editorial judgment, not a vote by mathematicians, a scholarly consensus, an objective difficulty score, or a list of problems that AI can most easily solve.
- Entries include individual conjectures, open problems, and conjecture families. The 100 entries are not 100 mutually disjoint atomic statements.
- The source distinguishes unresolved general cases, partial results, recent claims under review, disputed claims, and recent proof literature. Historical importance and present resolution status should be considered separately.
- Status notes reflect the edition date and the scope of its literature checks. Publishing these files does not independently verify later developments. Suggested AI-assisted directions are research proposals, not validated solution methods.

## The Three Volumes: Scope and Counting Rules

**Volume I** establishes what can be counted within a defined collection. It covers 17 subject categories and provides an index of 1,117 title-keyword matches and an index of 1,417 archived records. The main text contains 17,614 published records. Unique record identifiers do not establish complete mathematical or semantic deduplication.

**Volume II** expands the available search leads, primarily through MathDB public catalog excerpts and Formal Conjectures research statements. Screening uses Volume I as a reference, but text matching, similarity scores, and problem-family identification do not prove that every retained item is mathematically independent. Excerpts may omit conditions or parts of a conclusion.

**Volume III** includes 326 explicit conjectures and research questions, 17,579 historical and current OEIS mentions, and 2,455 forum and literature-location records. A separate appendix contains 9,342 parameterized problem instances. Historical mentions, discussion posts, bibliographic leads, and parameter instances serve different purposes and should be interpreted accordingly.

These figures describe **source-record counts**. They must not be added together and presented as the total number of mathematical conjectures or currently unsolved conjectures. Equivalent formulations, variants, historical status, and overlap across sources require further checking.

## Download and Verify

```sh
git clone https://github.com/ziyor-ai/Math-Conjectures-and-Open-Problems.git
cd Math-Conjectures-and-Open-Problems
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
```

On macOS, use `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS`. In Windows PowerShell, use `Get-FileHash *.pdf -Algorithm SHA256` and compare the results with [SHA256SUMS](SHA256SUMS).

## Citation and Feedback

When citing a specific problem, prioritize its original paper or database record and retain the version and access date. To cite these compilations, use the relevant entry below. Titles are translated into English for reference; the publications are in Chinese.

```text
Shen Yang (directing AI generation). AI's Top 100 Mathematical Conjectures: Detailed Explanations. 2026-10-24. [In Chinese]
Shen Yang (directing AI generation). How Many Mathematical Conjectures Are There? A Scale Assessment and Traceable Source Collection. 2026-10-25. [In Chinese]
Shen Yang (directing AI generation). Mathematical Conjectures and Open Problems, Volume II: A Supplementary Catalog Beyond Volume I. 2026-10-25. [In Chinese]
Shen Yang (directing AI generation). Mathematical Conjectures and Open Problems, Volume III: Multi-Source Supplements and Historical Mentions. 2026-10-25. [In Chinese]
Repository: https://github.com/ziyor-ai/Math-Conjectures-and-Open-Problems
```

To report an incorrect entry, broken source link, or change in research status, open an [issue](https://github.com/ziyor-ai/Math-Conjectures-and-Open-Problems/issues) with the document name, page or record identifier, a description of the problem, and a verifiable original source.
